items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: Big Spider-Beck completely lost in the Whiteman outfit

ctx.x: And that's not, that's the subject of mine.

Well, I, I feel that, uh, the, uh, other types of music, the men, they came on with the augmented bands, and the strict arrangements that cracked the style of the real, authentic musician like Muggsy Spanier playing in all these big bands, or Big Spider-Beck completely lost in the Whiteman outfit, that, that completely... jazz, you could come in, couldn't find a jazz band for 15, 20 years.

Well, uh, is that true in New Orleans? I mean, the, the normal small, say, three to, to eight pieces, the usual seven piece, six, six, seven piece, real, as good as jazz bands. Were they used, did the use of those tend to fall off during the, during the 20s of doing a duty?

items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: Now, I think how ashamed I ought to be because I love Big so much now.

ctx.x: I was in Chicago from 1921 to 1925. And one interesting thing that I did hear and I was not aware of what I was hearing was Charlie Strait's band at the rendezvous which I got a job He was. He was. And I remember a small group when the big band would quit these five fellas would stay on the bandstand. And it would consist of tuba, piano, drums, cornet and I don't remember which other instrument. But I remember the music was a little disturbing to me. It was not in the either dance idiom like the band was playing…
Probably some of his in the mist type of thing.
